sections.description: Frames the patient’s timeline and the disease mechanisms that made a third transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV) both necessary and technically challenging.
subtopics: Patient timeline: Lotus (2014) for native severe AS → Evolut TAV-in-TAV (2022) → Enterococcus faecalis prosthetic valve endocarditis (treated) → recurrent severe prosthetic dysfunction (2024) → third TAVI (Acurate neo2, 2024); 1-year outcome

Comorbidity and risk profile shaping therapy: multivessel CAD with prior PCI, AV block with pacemaker, COPD, diabetes, prior vascular complication, recurrent GI bleeding; high surgical risk (EuroSCORE II ~27%)

Mechanisms of transcatheter prosthesis failure: structural valve deterioration (leaflet fibrosis/calcification), infection-related leaflet injury/restriction, hemodynamic consequences of serial frames

Key hazards unique to serial TAV-in-TAV (and TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV): reduced effective orifice area and prosthesis–patient mismatch (PPM), coronary obstruction risk, commissural misalignment with impaired future coronary access, frame interaction/underexpansion

sections.description: Details the clinical assessment, differential diagnosis of prosthetic valve dysfunction, infection clearance, and the multimodality imaging strategy (especially CT) that enabled a safe, feasible third TAVI.
subtopics: Clinical presentation in 2024: exertional dyspnea, dizziness, fatigue; TTE showing severe stenosis (mean gradient ~49 mmHg), AVA 0.5 cm², moderate-to-severe intraprosthetic AR; EF 66%

Differential diagnosis of transcatheter prosthesis dysfunction: structural degeneration vs leaflet thrombosis vs recurrent endocarditis vs PPM/malposition; aligning echo findings with clinical context

Excluding active infection before reintervention: repeated negative blood cultures, TEE without vegetations/paravalvular complications, MSCT without abscess; completion of targeted E. faecalis therapy and clinical resolution
Echocardiographic quantification: AVA by continuity equation, gradients, Doppler Velocity Index; interpreting metrics in the setting of serial bioprostheses

MSCT for feasibility and coronary safety: minimal internal diameter of the in-situ valve (13.7 mm) confirming severe compromise; measuring coronary ostial heights, sinus of Valsalva, valve-to-coronary (VTC) distance, anticipated neo-skirt, and frame–frame interactions
Planning commissural alignment and high implantation to preserve coronary flow and future access; rationale for proceeding without coronary protection based on CT-derived distances and modeling

Heart-team decision-making and surgical risk: prior frames deeply integrated in the aortic root, prohibitive risk of surgical explant/root replacement; individualized strategy favored transcatheter redo

sections.section_title: Third TAVI Strategy and Execution (Acurate neo2 in a Double-Framed Anatomy)
sections.description: Explains the procedural plan, device choice, implantation technique, and risk-mitigation tactics tailored to a triple-stented aortic root.
subtopics: Access and setup: local anesthesia; left femoral arterial access for device delivery; left radial access for aortography; pigtail confirmation of severe AR
Hemodynamic support maneuvers: Safari wire to LV; rapid ventricular pacing (≈180 bpm) for ballooning and deployment
Predilation and coronary assessment: 22/40 mm balloon under pacing; simultaneous aortography to confirm unobstructed coronary flow

Device selection rationale: self-expanding Acurate neo2 (size S) for supra-annular leaflet position, favorable hemodynamics in small/narrow internal diameters, relatively low frame height, and commissural alignment capability

High implantation and leaflet ‘tacking’ strategy: aligning with Evolut leaflets to prevent inward leaflet folding, maximize effective orifice, and minimize a neo-skirt below coronary ostia to preserve flow and access
Postdilation and optimization: 20/40 mm balloon under pacing to improve expansion and leaflet motion; potential partial radial expansion of the prior frame without intentional valve-fracture
Commissural alignment: CT-based orientation and fluoroscopic landmarks to reduce future coronary access complexity

Risk mitigation and bailouts considered: indications for (but ultimately not used) coronary protection or BASILICA; awareness of complications—coronary obstruction, annular/aortic injury, conduction issues, vascular access complications, stroke—and preventive steps

sections.description: Interprets immediate and longitudinal results using standardized criteria, explains early gradients, and contextualizes the 1-year findings.
subtopics: Immediate procedural success (VARC-3): correct position, no PVL or transvalvular AR, preserved coronary flow, no major complications
Early hemodynamics: high mean gradient (≈67 mmHg), AVA 0.9 cm², DVI 0.24—severe PPM in the early phase
Mechanisms for early high gradients with serial frames: transient underexpansion, multi-frame compliance, flow recovery dynamics; expected improvement after optimization and physiologic remodeling
Trajectory of improvement: at 1 month, mean gradient ~27 mmHg, AVA ~1.1 cm², no AR; LV reverse remodeling

Durability to 1 year: mean gradient ~26 mmHg, AVA ~1.1 cm², EF ~65%, asymptomatic, no reinfection—interpretation as acceptable moderate stenosis in a triple-stented anatomy with sustained clinical benefit

Follow-up surveillance principles: serial TTE (baseline post-procedure, 1–3 months, 6–12 months, then annually), clinical checks for heart failure or infection recurrence, and consideration of CT if deterioration occurs

sections.section_title: Clinical Lessons, Decision Pathways, and Lifetime Management
sections.description: Synthesizes takeaways into actionable guidance for selecting candidates, planning procedures, preserving future options, and monitoring long term—especially after treated prosthetic valve endocarditis.
subtopics: Candidacy for TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV: prerequisites—controlled/eradicated infection, acceptable CT-derived coronary safety margins, feasible implant depth and alignment plan, target effective orifice acceptable, prohibitive surgical risk, heart-team consensus and informed patient choice

Imaging checklist: measure internal valve diameters, coronary ostial heights, sinus dimensions, VTC and valve-to-sinotubular junction distances; model anticipated neo-skirt and frame overlap; plan cusp-overlap view and commissural alignment; anticipate coronary reaccess routes

Device and technique principles: favor supra-annular leaflet design and frame geometry that limit additional height/mesh; aim for high implantation when safe; reserve coronary protection/BASILICA for borderline VTC or unfavorable sinus anatomy; consider (but weigh) valve fracture when expansion is limiting

Managing prior PVE: ensure completed, targeted antimicrobial therapy; document negative cultures and no imaging signs of active infection; no routine need for chronic suppressive antibiotics if infection is eradicated; apply standard endocarditis prevention measures thereafter

Long-term planning and constraints: cumulative mesh may hinder future coronary interventions; document commissural orientation and frame positions; set realistic expectations about limited future options and the potential difficulty of surgical explant
Evidence gaps and research needs: paucity of data on TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV after treated PVE; the value of CT-driven protocols, alignment strategies, and registries to refine safety and durability
